content.comment_body: The [product_name] [version_no] is sufficient for programming the latest [product_name] hardware revision [version_no]. When selecting hardware, choose the [product_name] with the corresponding hardware revision. You only need the newest [product_name] [version_no] if you have the latest operator device with a new [article_no] and plan to configure it on the network using the updated software.
What about [product_name] [version_no]? Can [product_name] hardware from [version_no] and earlier be programmed using [product_name] [version_no]?
With [product_name] [version_no], it's possible to create or modify programs for all [product_name] hardware, from the earliest hardware revision to the newest one.

I want to clarify: newer [product_name] CPUs such as [product_name] [version_no] and later can't be programmed using [product_name] [version_no]. Are these newer CPUs supported only by the most recent software version, or can the older version still be used for programming?

analysis.insight_summary: Users are discussing compatibility between different versions of [product_name] software and various hardware revisions. The primary concern is which hardware versions are supported by each software version, particularly for newer CPUs and operator devices. There is uncertainty regarding whether software upgrades are necessary to work with newly released hardware, and about backward or forward compatibility.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect clear information about hardware and software compatibility, specifically if updated CPUs and operator devices require the newest software version. They want straightforward programming across hardware and software generations without issues.
